title: A steel bar held at its ends and heated past yield (small strain)
source: Uniaxial J2 plasticity with linear hardening (Simo and Hughes, Computational Inelasticity, Springer 1998, §2.3) with the additive thermal strain: the bar's total axial strain is held at zero, so its mechanical strain is −α ΔT and σ = −(σ_y + E_t (α ΔT − σ_y/E)) once α ΔT exceeds σ_y/E

quantities.quantity: axial stress, ΔT = 300 (α ΔT = 3.6·10⁻³, 2.9 times the yield strain)
quantities.reason: a homogeneous uniaxial state the elements represent exactly
